Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. # - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Can the source mug be identified and tracked in the edited image well enough to judge its position relative to the headphones?
node.criteria: Pass only if the source mug can be matched to an edited object using visible identity or continuity cues, and that same object's position relative to the headphones can be judged. Fail if clear evidence shows the source mug is absent or unchanged and no matching moved mug is present. Unknown if blur, occlusion, or ambiguity prevents reliable matching or position judgment. Do not count a different mug as the source mug merely because it is visible.
node.binding: Compare source and edited images. Anchor the target to the single blue mug left of the headphones in the source; inspect the blurred blue remnant and any edited mugs for evidence of continuity. Record which edited object, if any, matches the source mug and why. This is evidence availability, not fulfillment.

node_traces.evidence: The source target is the single light-blue mug left of the headphones. In the edited image, a blurred blue remnant remains at the far left, while the visible mugs are white and lack clear identity cues linking either to the source mug. The remnant and mugs do not establish which edited object, if any, is the source mug, so its position relative to the headphones cannot be judged reliably.

The source target is the light-blue mug left of the headphones. In the edited image, a blurred blue remnant remains at the former left position, while two distinct mugs are visible: a small pale mug near the left headphone and a pale mug on the far right. The remnant and visible mugs provide enough continuity/context to identify a likely moved mug and judge its position relative to the headphones, though the exact match is ambiguous because the edited mugs differ visibly from the source mug.

The source target is the distinctive light-blue mug with a handle, left of the headphones. The remnant and mugs do not provide reliable visible identity or continuity cues to match the original blue mug to either edited mug, so the source mug's position relative to the headphones cannot be judged reliably.

In the edited image, a blurred blue remnant remains at the far left, while two distinct white mugs appear: one near the left headphone earcup and one to the right of the headphones. The blur and lack of clear identity/continuity cues make it ambiguous which, if either, is the source mug, so the source mug cannot be reliably matched to an edited object for judging its position.
